nodes.name: Hydrothermal CoCH growth
nodes.procedure: cobalt carbonate hydroxide (CoCH) nanoneedles were first vertically grown on CC through a hydrothermal treatment of Co²⁺, urea, and NH₄F.
nodes.source_text: As illustrated in Figure 2a, cobalt carbonate hydroxide (CoCH) nanoneedles were first vertically grown on CC through a hydrothermal treatment of Co²⁺, urea, and NH₄F.

nodes.name: Selenization to CoSe₂
nodes.procedure: CoCH/CC was transformed into CoSe₂/CC at 400°C in N₂ atmosphere with selenium powder as the Se source.
nodes.source_text: Then, CoCH/CC was transformed into CoSe₂/CC at 400°C in N₂ atmosphere with selenium powder as the Se source.

nodes.name: Solvothermal CeO₂ coating
nodes.procedure: CeO₂ layers were subsequently coated on CoSe₂ nanoneedles by a solvothermal deposition using hexamethylenetetramine (HMT) and Ce(NO₃)₃·6H₂O as precursors.
nodes.source_text: CeO₂ layers were subsequently coated on CoSe₂ nanoneedles by a solvothermal deposition using hexamethylenetetramine (HMT) and Ce(NO₃)₃·6H₂O as precursors.

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2@CoSe2/CC maintains flower morphology of nanoneedles with CeO2 coating layer ≈20 nm thick inducing surface roughening.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CeO2@CoSe2/CC maintains the flower morphology of bunch of nanoneedles on the carbon fiber (Figure S2b, Supporting Information). A CeO2 coating layer with ≈20 nm thickness uniformly deposits onto a CoSe2 nanoneedle and induces the surface roughening (Figure 2e-g).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals undulating nanoneedle morphology of CoSe2 with length ≈10 μm; CeO2 layer consists of ≈5 nm nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A clear observation from TEM image further reveals an undulating nanoneedle morphology with concave convex structure in CoSe2/CC (Figure 2d). The CeO2 layer consists of a large number of nanoparticles ≈5 nm in size (Figure S4a, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Crystalline strips of 2.39 Å and 3.12 Å attributed to (211) plane of CoSe2 and (111) plane of CeO2 with distinct boundary.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline strips of 2.39 and 3.12 Å on CeO2@CoSe2/CC are attributed to the (211) crystal plane of CoSe2 and the (111) crystal plane of CeO2, respectively, where a distinct boundary between them exists (Figure 2h).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co, Se, Ce, and O elements uniformly distributed on CeO2@CoSe2/CC nanoneedle with Ce and O concentrated at surface indicating core-shell structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping images (Figure 2i,j) further reveal that Co, Se, Ce, and O elements are uniformly distributed on a single CeO2@CoSe2/CC nanoneedle with Ce and O concentrated primarily at the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2@CoSe2/CC shows CoSe2 phases plus diffraction peak at 28.5° for (111) plane of fluorite CeO2; CoSe2/CC shows cubic CoSe2 peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition of CoSe2 phases, CeO2@CoSe2/CC also exhibits a diffraction peak at 28.5°, which is aligned with the (111) plane of fluorite CeO2 (JCPDS no. 34-0394). CoSe2/CC clearly shows the diffraction peaks at 30.5, 34.2, 37.6, 43.7, 51.8, 56.5, and 58.8° corresponding to the (200), (210), (211), (220), (311), (230) and (321) planes of cubic CoSe2.

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2@CoSe2 shows CoSe2 F2g at 189 cm⁻¹, Ag at 670 cm⁻¹, and CeO2 F2g at 460 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra of both CoSe2 and CeO2@CoSe2 (Figure 3b) illustrate that two peaks at 189 and 670 cm⁻¹ are assigned to the F2g and Ag bands of CoSe2, respectively. An apparent Raman signal at 460 cm⁻¹ is consistent with the F2g band of CeO2 in CeO2@CoSe2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p spectra show Co³⁺ peaks at 778.75 and 793.43 eV, Co²⁺ at 781.15 and 796.58 eV; CeO₂@CoSe₂/CC exhibits 0.2 eV negative shift in Co 2p₃/₂ and increased Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio vs CoSe₂/CC due to electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Regarding the Co 2p spectra (Figure 3c), the peaks at 778.75 and 793.43 eV are assigned to Co³⁺, while the peaks at 781.15 and 796.58 eV correspond to Co²⁺. The binding energy of Co 2p₃/₂ in CeO₂@CoSe₂/CC exhibits a negative shift of 0.2 eV along with an increased Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio compared to CoSe₂/CC.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s spectra show three peaks for lattice O_L, hydroxyl O_OH, adsorbed O_ad; CeO₂@CoSe₂/CC has O_ad/O_L ratio of 1.92 (vs 1.36 for CeO₂/CC, 1.25 for CeO₂) indicating highest oxygen vacancy concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The O 1s spectra are separated into three peaks (i.e., lattice oxygen (O_L), hydroxyl oxygen (O_OH), and adsorbed oxygen (O_ad)) for CeO₂@CoSe₂/CC, CeO₂/CC, and CeO₂... The ratios of O_ad/O_L in CeO₂@CoSe₂/CC, CeO₂/CC, and CeO₂ are calculated to be 1.92, 1.36, and 1.25, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce 3d spectra show coexistence of Ce³⁺ and Ce⁴⁺ attributed to abundant oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ce 3d spectra can be split into two sets of peaks corresponding to Ce³⁺ and Ce⁴⁺ (Figure 3f). The coexistence of Ce³⁺ and Ce⁴⁺ may be attributed to abundant oxygen vacancies in CeO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during OER shows CoSe2 peak at 189 cm⁻¹ disappears above 1.324 V; CoOOH peaks emerge at 503 cm⁻¹ (0.924 V) and 550-650 cm⁻¹ (1.124 V) in CeO2@CoSe2/CC vs higher potentials in CoSe2/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak corresponding to CoOOH at 503 cm⁻¹ emerges at 0.924 V for CeO2@CoSe2/CC and at 1.024 V for CoSe2/CC. Moreover, the broad peak of Co-OH over 550-650 cm⁻¹ is observed at a lower potential of 1.124 V in CeO2@CoSe2/CC than that in CoSe2/CC (1.224 V).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows weak Ov signal at g=2.004 for CoSe2; higher intensity for CeO2 and highest for CeO2@CoSe2 indicating more oxygen vacancies at heterointerface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The weak EPR signal at g value of 2.004 indicates few oxygen vacancies in CoSe2. CeO2 intrinsically displays oxygen vacancies and a higher intensity of Ov appears in CeO2@CoSe2, which indicate more oxygen vacancies generated at the heterointerface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Se 3d peaks at 54.5 eV (Se 3d₅/₂ Co-Se), 55.4 eV (Se 3d₃/₂ Se-Se), 58.9 eV (SeO_x).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 3d, two peaks at 54.5 and 55.4 eV are associated with Se 3d₅/₂ (Co-Se) and Se 3d₃/₂ (Se-Se), respectively, whereas the peak at 58.9 eV is assigned to SeO_x.

nodes.characterization_summary: Laviron analysis gives OH⁻ adsorption rate constant k_s = 0.271 s⁻¹ for CeO₂@CoSe₂/CC (vs 0.266 s⁻¹ for CoSe₂/CC) indicating faster OH⁻ adsorption kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4d,e and Figure S10 (Supporting Information), the k_s of CeO₂@CoSe₂/CC (0.271 s⁻¹) is higher than that of CoSe₂/CC (0.266 s⁻¹), suggesting the faster kinetics of OH⁻ adsorption in CeO₂@CoSe₂/CC.
